data.title: Benzoyl peroxide (2.5–5%)
data.summary: VII Anti-acne — Others · Oxidising agent; bactericidal, keratolytic
data.body:
_Topicals · VII Anti-acne — Others_

**Class:** Oxidising agent; bactericidal, keratolytic

## Mechanism of action
- Releases free oxygen radicals inside the follicle → kills C. acnes (bactericidal)
- Bacteria cannot develop resistance (non-specific oxidation)
- Mild comedolytic and anti-inflammatory effects

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Acne vulgaris — in nearly every regimen; combine with topical/oral antibiotics to prevent resistance
- Pitted keratolysis, folliculitis, decolonisation (washes)

## Dose & formulations
- 2.5–5% gel once or twice daily (2.5% is as effective as 10% with less irritation)
- Washes 4–10%: short-contact for chest/back
- Fixed combinations: BPO + clindamycin, BPO + adapalene

## Adverse effects
- Dryness, peeling, redness, burning
- Bleaches hair, clothes, towels and bed linen
- Allergic contact dermatitis (about 1%)

## Contraindications
- Known allergy; acutely inflamed skin

## Drug interactions
- Oxidises tretinoin (apply at different times) — adapalene is stable
- Combined use with dapsone gel can cause temporary orange-brown skin discolouration

## Pregnancy & lactation
Safe (minimal absorption).

## Viva points
- No antibiotic resistance — the reason it is combined with antibiotics
- 2.5% works as well as higher strengths with less irritation
- Bleaches fabrics — counsel patients

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.41 (BPO) and ch.46; Khopkar ch.18. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
